title: Grateful Dead Live at Fillmore West on 1970-06-06
source: SBD -> Master Reel -> Cassette -> Dat -> CD

ai_review.summary: An excellent Charlie Miller sound‑board capture of the June 6 1970 Fillmore West show, highlighted by a smoking Alligator jam, blistering New Orleans, and a flawless Lovelight → Not Fade Away transition.
ai_review.review: The Miller SBD transfer delivers crystal‑clear sound that lets the band’s fireworks shine – from Jerry’s searing Alligator guitar to the tight, locked‑in drumming throughout the hour‑long jam sequence.  Highlights include the Dancin’ groove, a rare New Orleans, an epic Lovelight → Not Fade Away → Lovelight stretch and an Attics of My Life that many call the best ever, while the encore’s Uncle John’s Band suffers from a mix glitch.  Overall the performance is rated among the very best of 1970.

ai_rating.rationale: The majority of reviews (15+) are 4‑5 stars and praise both the musical performance and the Miller soundboard transfer; only a few note minor mix issues, yielding an overall high combined rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Charlie Miller’s SBD is described as crisp, fantastic and well‑balanced; several reviewers call it one of the best‑sounding 1970 transfers, with only occasional comments that it isn’t quite as sharp as a few other dates.

show_quality.setlist_flow: The second set is jam‑heavy and flows brilliantly, building from the post‑Alligator marathon into a hour‑long Lovelight sequence; the first set provides solid acoustic highlights (Candyman, Friend of the Devil) but the encore suffers from mix glitches.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Praised for searing guitar on the Alligator jam and tight interplay with Bob; a brief drop‑out in the UJB outro is noted.
band_member_comments.Bob: His rhythm work shines, especially during the post‑Alligator drums and the Lovelight melodic section.
band_member_comments.Drums: Drummers are highlighted as locked‑in, with standout drum brakes and a superb Darkness jam.
